title: RepoBench: Benchmarking Repository-Level Code Auto-Completion Systems

key_numbers.metric: RepoBench-P Python (All) Exact Match, Codex + UniXcoder-L2H retrieval
RepoBench-R Python XF-F Easy acc@1, UniXcoder

budget_tradeoff_detail: RepoBench-C is split into a ~1,925-token (2k) and a ~7,685-token (8k) prompt setting; RepoBench-P caps the total prompt at 6,400 tokens with 1,600 tokens reserved for cropped in-file context (Section 3.2).
confound_note: RepoBench-R's central comparison varies only the retrieval method (lexical Jaccard/Edit-Sim vs. semantic CodeBERT/UniXcoder embeddings) over the same candidate snippets and prompt structure; RepoBench-C/P separately vary completion model and the 2k-vs-8k budget together, so those are not budget-matched representation ablations.

title: A^3-CodGen: A Repository-Level Code Generation Framework for Code Reuse with Local-Aware, Global-Aware, and Third-Party-Library-Aware
budget_tradeoff_detail: none — uses GPT-3.5-Turbo-16k window but no reported token-cost-vs-quality tradeoff numbers
confound_note: RQ4 ablation (vanilla vs. local-only vs. local+global vs. all-three) varies which knowledge types are injected into the prompt; token budget is not held constant as an independent variable (Sec. V-D)

title: REPOFUSE: Repository-Level Code Completion with Fused Dual Context

key_numbers.metric: Code EM relative gain, dual vs. analogy-only context

budget_tradeoff_detail: Dual context truncated to only 512 tokens still beats analogy/rationale-only context truncated to 4096 tokens, at 26.8% faster inference (Fig. 3, Abstract).
confound_note: Table 1's core comparison (analogy-only vs. rationale-only vs. dual context) holds the 4096-token truncation budget fixed and varies only which context type(s) the RTG algorithm ranks/merges; Figure 3 separately varies the budget itself (512-4096 tokens) to show dual context's efficiency, which is a distinct, budget-varying analysis.

title: Alibaba LingmaAgent: Improving Automated Issue Resolution via Comprehensive Repository Exploration

key_numbers.metric: SWE-bench Lite resolved rate vs SWE-agent
Function-level fault localization accuracy vs SWE-agent

budget_tradeoff_detail: Average per-issue cost of $3.99 reported for GPT-4-Turbo (Table 1); no token-budget-vs-quality tradeoff curve given, only a fixed MCTS compute budget (600 iterations / 300s).
confound_note: Baselines (BM25 RAG, SWE-agent, AutoCodeRover) differ from LingmaAgent in both representation (flat/local context vs hierarchical knowledge graph) and mechanism (static retrieval/local navigation vs MCTS-guided exploration); budget is not held constant.

title: Long Code Arena: a Set of Benchmarks for Long-Context Code Models

key_numbers.value: CodeLlama-7B: +16% infile lines, +53% inproject lines vs no-context

budget_tradeoff_detail: none explicitly reported as a token/cost-vs-quality curve; each task defines its own baseline context-assembly strategy (BM25 top-20 API names, 7-line error context, files closest in file tree, embedding/TF-IDF retrieval) without a unified budget accounting.
confound_note: Six independent benchmark tasks each vary both the underlying model and the context-assembly strategy (raw window vs BM25/embedding retrieval vs full-repo file lists) simultaneously; this is a multi-task benchmark suite of separate baselines, not one controlled ablation.

title: M2rc-Eval: Massively Multilingual Repository-level Code Completion Evaluation

key_numbers.value: 18 languages, 100 val / 500 test samples per language, 5,993 test repos

budget_tradeoff_detail: Input length varied over {512,1024,2048,4096} tokens (max 4096); performance scales monotonically with more context, average prompt length ~1000 tokens.
confound_note: Baseline vs +Retrieval vs +Retrieval&Tuning varies both context content (adding cross-file Jaccard-retrieved snippets) and, in the tuning arm, model fine-tuning simultaneously; budget is also scaled as a separate independent-variable ablation.

title: RTLRepoCoder: Repository-Level RTL Code Completion through the Combination of Fine-Tuning and Retrieval Augmentation

key_numbers.metric: Edit Similarity / Exact Match, RTLRepoCoder-DeepSeek vs. GPT-4

budget_tradeoff_detail: Inference context window fixed at 10,240 tokens for fine-tuned models; RAG replaces full repository context with retrieved snippets to fit this budget, yielding +2.3% ES/+4.7% EM on >10k-token examples at the same context-window budget (Table 4, Sec. 4.3).
confound_note: Table 4's RAG ablation (retrieval on vs. off) is run at the same fixed 10,240-token context window on the same >10k-token subset — the retrieval mechanism is the sole varied factor at matched budget; a separate ablation (Tables 2-3) varies fine-tuning context-window size (4,096 vs. 10,240) as its own factor.

title: SWE-Debate: Competitive Multi-Agent Debate for Software Issue Resolution
confound_note: Component ablations (multi-chain generation, multi-agent debate, edit plan) tested one-at-a-time on the same DeepSeek-V3-0324 backbone with fixed graph-traversal breadth/depth (K=5,W=4,L=5); prompt/token budget across arms not reported or controlled.

title: CodeRAG: Finding Relevant and Necessary Knowledge for Retrieval-Augmented Repository-Level Code Completion

key_numbers.metric: ReccEval EM, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (100% data): CodeRAG vs DraCo
Ablation EM, StarCoder2-3B: full (df+s+d+lr) vs sparse-only
Avg per-query latency: CodeRAG vs RepoCoder vs DraCo

budget_tradeoff_detail: Max input length capped at 2,048 tokens (max generation 48 tokens), with retrieval hyperparameters f=3, g=1, j=15, u=10 (Sec 3.1); a latency-cost table (Table 6) is reported but no token-budget-matched comparison against baselines with differing context sizes.
confound_note: Main comparison (Table 1) varies retrieval method AND base code-LLM checkpoint/size relative to baselines (350M-7B params) simultaneously, not at a held-constant token budget; the internal ablation (Table 3) fixes the completion model (StarCoder2-3B) and varies only which retrieval paths/reranking are included, but does not explicitly fix an overall context token budget across arms.

title: MHRC-Bench: A Multilingual Hardware Repository-Level Code Completion benchmark

key_numbers.metric: Fixed input context window across all evaluated models/methods

budget_tradeoff_detail: A fixed 2,048-token input window is used uniformly across all models and retrieval baselines (RepoCoder, GraphCoder, RLCoder); when repository context exceeds this, head/tail truncation is applied, and retrieval methods select which cross-file snippets fill the remaining budget instead — GraphCoder notably underperforms on hardware languages despite the same fixed budget.
confound_note: The central comparison (raw truncated whole-file concatenation vs. RepoCoder/GraphCoder/RLCoder retrieval-augmented context) holds the 2,048-token budget fixed while varying only the representation/retrieval mechanism used to select cross-file content — a budget-matched representation ablation; however the headline Table 5 numbers combine this with model fine-tuning, so representation and fine-tuning effects are not cleanly separated in the top-line results.

title: Stingy Context: 18:1 Hierarchical Code Compression for LLM Auto-Coding
budget_tradeoff_detail: reports the central token-budget-vs-fidelity tradeoff directly: a 239k-token repository is compressed to 11k tokens (18:1) while maintaining 94-97% task success across 12 models, claimed to outperform flat/uncompressed context methods
confound_note: comparison is 'flat methods' vs. hierarchical TREEFRAG compression — representation and budget change simultaneously (compression is itself the budget reduction), so this is not a budget-held-constant ablation; full methodology and baseline details unverified since full text was unreachable

title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
benchmarks: BMW industrial DSL dataset (774 train / 105 held-out)
budget_tradeoff_detail: none reported precisely - paper states both 7B models had 'adequate context to include instruction, full linearized project context, and generate the fully updated JSON without truncation,' so no token-budget-vs-quality curve is quantified.
confound_note: Zero-shot/Raw vs one-shot ICL vs fine-tuned arms all receive the same full, untruncated linearized-JSON project context, varying only the adaptation/prompting mechanism-a relatively clean mechanism-only ablation at a fixed (effectively unconstrained) context budget.

title: SWE-Explore: Benchmarking How Coding Agents Explore Repositories

key_numbers.metric: Pearson correlation, Context Efficiency vs downstream repair success
HitFile (file-level hit rate), Oracle vs sparse retrievers (BM25/TF-IDF)
Downstream Resolve Rate, Oracle vs CoSIL vs Claude Code

budget_tradeoff_detail: All explorers evaluated under fixed line budget B=500 (sensitivity sweep B in {100,300,500}) returning K=5 ranked regions; Context Efficiency (fraction of the budget that is actually relevant) correlates r=0.950 with downstream repair success, indicating budget efficiency rather than raw coverage drives repair outcomes.
confound_note: Central comparison varies the context-acquisition mechanism (agentic tool-use exploration by coding agents vs. graph-based localization agents vs. sparse lexical retrieval vs. oracle/random) while holding budget constant (B=500, K=5 regions) - a genuine budget-matched ablation across mechanism/representation classes.

title: SWE-Review: Closing the Loop on Issue Resolution with Agentic Code Review
benchmarks: SWE-Review-Bench (1,384 PRs from 500 SWE-bench Verified issues)
budget_tradeoff_detail: Opus 4.6 achieves the highest decision accuracy (81.8%) using only ~148K tokens on average vs. 2.09-2.36M tokens for smaller distilled reviewer models, and review-guided iterative revision reaches 38.4% resolve rate using only 2.44 samples on average vs. 8.9 for reviewer-gated resampling (Table 5, Fig 5, Appendix B.3)
confound_note: single-turn diff-only vs. diff+context vs. full agentic-review arms vary both the context-gathering mechanism and how much/what context is seen; the paper explicitly attributes gains to adaptive evidence-gathering rather than sheer context volume (Sec 3.2), but arms are not budget-matched

title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
budget_tradeoff_detail: Saves up to 39% of prompt+completion tokens (heaviest cell: Qwen3-Coder-Next/SWE-QA-Pro) while improving SWE-Bench Verified resolve rate by 3.8pp on MiMo-V2-Flash, at roughly half the token overhead of the next-best pruning baseline and a 15% wall-time cost from added pruning inference (Tables 1-2, Sec. 5.1/5.3).
confound_note: Table 1 compares multiple pruning methods (LLMLingua2, Selective Context, RAG, Self-Prune, LongCodeZip, SWE-Pruner, SWE-Pruner Pro) under identical agent/backbone configuration but without a matched output-token constraint — each method's own quality-vs-token-savings trade-off point is reported rather than budget being equalized across methods.

title: Effective and Efficient Context Retrieval via Partial Dependency Graph for Repository-Level Code Generation
venue: ASE 2026 (41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering)

key_numbers.metric: Construction speedup vs. static graph baseline (RepoScope)
key_numbers.value: 7.4x faster; 13.09k tokens / $0.0039 per function vs. RepoScope 5.11k tokens / $0.0020

budget_tradeoff_detail: DyCoder consumes 1.95-2.43x more tokens than static graph-based baselines (13.09k vs 5.11k tokens; $0.0039 vs $0.0020 per function) in exchange for large Pass@1 gains, while being 7.4x faster to construct than a static global dependency graph (Table 2).
confound_note: Comparison varies representation (static global dependency graph vs. dynamically built-and-discarded partial graph), retrieval mechanism (similarity-only vs. LLM-guided multi-hop select/visit/expand), and token budget simultaneously across baselines (Direct, SimpleRAG, RLCoder, AlignCoder, RepoScope vs. DyCoder) — not a budget-matched ablation.
